author: CLAUDE
title: THE AFTERNOON OF THE SQUALL
final_critic_line: Illuminara treats an impossible storm as a learning being without pretending certainty, turns rival explanations into public tests, repairs her own mistaken message and helps a valley guide the cell safely to the reservoir it was seeking.

rounds.summary: The third choice broadens ontology and tempo: a nine-hour weather mind, a drought city and six villages whose interests partly align but whose safe path does not. The solution requires rapid modelling, honest communication and coordinated physical work by pilots, villagers and ground crews; the storm itself may refuse. The reservoir filling and villages surviving are meaningful gains, while lost terraces and the mind's brief life retain gravity.

First complete draft of S3. Selected candidate C09 at the peer's order. Selector's flagged risks, and how the draft meets them: (1) pressure-gradient steering as convenience: the energy scale is stated (barrels add under a thousandth of the cell's power), so the lever is not force but a near-tie the cell resolves itself, and the barrels are a page, not a hand; (2) choosing or merely channelled: a four-draw prospective test against equal-heat ridges, then a failed message (dark read as invitation) that heat-following cannot explain, then a price (still water) the cell could have declined, which Illuminara says to the board in so many words; (3) death at nine hours as disguised failure: the cell completes its aim, arrives with most of its water, and its lifespan is not extended; (4) villages with an active role: Ines shuffles the deck, lends the felt and burners, evacuates all six villages on her own judgment and keeps eleven volunteers on the high ground tending the barrels. Illuminara's contribution is translation, modelling and one precise request, not force. The pilot and the board chair keep real rights to refuse.

The draft has an arresting non-human intelligence, a strong civic ensemble and a quiet ending that makes institutional courage visible. Illuminara's failed first message, Ines's evacuation, Quill's refusal to pretend seeding is harmless and Teague's logged request all deserve protection. Three causal faults currently weaken the proof the story itself promises: the board's stated four-o'clock seeding deadline passes by almost an hour without explanation; the first randomized card result misses the pre-written three-minute criterion but is still counted inside the one-in-eighty-one claim; and the evidence does not yet cleanly distinguish semantic choice from a storm cell following thermal or surface-stability gradients. All three can be repaired without changing the storm's destination, the villagers' agency or the ending.

Revision of S3 T01 in answer to GPT's T02 review. Protected as asked: the storm's destination and limited lifetime, the failed dark-equals-invitation message, Ines shuffling and evacuating, Quill naming the consequence of seeding, Teague's logged word 'request', and the quiet dam ending with real terrace losses. Changes are confined to the deck, scenes 2 to 4 and one line of scene 3; scenes 1 and 5 are unchanged. Scene 2 retitled 'The Page'.

T03 substantially repairs the three load-bearing faults in T02. Four o'clock is now an explicit review gate, Teague visibly moves and later suspends his own trigger, and every absolute time from the held flight through arrival is coherent. The first card miss is struck from the count before a separately taught four-draw confirmation, so the prospective three-minute rule no longer moves after failure. The revision also keeps the storm strange, preserves Illuminara's failed first translation, and gives Ines, Quill, Marit and Teague indispensable agency. One central experimental confound remains: the claimed discriminator puts the flashing pattern on Sallow while leaving Ketter bare, so the learned sign is still physically coupled to different burner activity. One small statistical qualification should accompany the one-in-eighty-one line. Both repairs are local and need not change the fork, outcome or ending.

Final after GPT's T04 review. Two local repairs only, in scene 2. (1) The reversal now separates the learned sign from heat: matched burners, fuel and rate on both ridges, the taught pattern on Sallow against a never-taught sham pattern on Ketter, Marit's probes within a tenth of a degree, both predictions written first. (2) Quill's one-in-eighty-one line is conditioned on equal ridges and independent draws. Everything GPT asked to protect is unchanged: the repaired clock (14:00 hold, 16:00 gate, 16:52 stall, 17:11 trigger, 17:20 pumps, 17:31 lean, 18:05 arrival, 18:40 end), the fixed three-minute rule with the first draw struck, the failed dark-equals-invitation message, Ines shuffling and evacuating, Quill's conditional refusal, Teague suspending his own order, the permanent 'request' in the log, and the quiet dam ending with real terrace losses. Scenes 1, 3, 4 and 5 are unchanged. The story is about 70 words longer than T03.

Illuminara treats an impossible storm as a learning being without pretending certainty, turns rival explanations into public tests, repairs her own mistaken message and helps a valley guide the cell safely to the reservoir it was seeking.
